dhp129:1: All men tremble at the rod; all men fear death.
dhp129:3: One should treat one’s neighbor as oneself, and therefore neither strike nor kill.
dhp130:1: All men tremble at the rod; to all men life is dear.
dhp130:3: One should treat one’s neighbor as oneself, and should neither strike nor kill.
dhp131:1: Whoever injures with the rod living beings that long for happiness,
dhp131:3: Longing himself for happiness, will not obtain happiness after death.
dhp132:1: Whoever does not injure with the rod living beings that long for happiness,
dhp132:3: Longing himself for happiness, will obtain happiness after death.
dhp133:1: Speak not harshly to anyone; those you address may answer you;
dhp133:3: For angry words bring trouble; blows for blows may touch you.
dhp134:1: If you keep yourself silent as a broken gong,
dhp134:3: You have already reached Nibbāna; angry speech is not found in you.
dhp135:1: As with a staff a cowherd drives his cows to pasture,
dhp135:3: Even so old age and death drive the life of living beings.
dhp136:1: In the act of committing wicked deeds, the simpleton does not realize their wickedness;
dhp136:3: But the stupid man is consumed by his own wicked deeds, as if burnt with fire.
dhp137:1: Whosoever visits punishment upon those that deserve not punishment,
dhp137:2: Whosoever offends against those that are without offense,
dhp137:3: Such an one will right quickly come to one of ten states:
dhp138:1: He will incur cruel suffering, or infirmity or injury of the body,
dhp138:3: Or severe sickness, or loss of mind,
dhp139:1: Or misfortune proceeding from the king, or a heavy accusation,
dhp139:3: Or death of relatives, or loss of treasures,
dhp140:1: Or else the fire of lightning will consume his houses;
dhp140:3: Upon dissolution of the body such a simpleton will go to Hell.
dhp141:1: Neither going naked, nor matted locks, nor filth, nor fasting, nor sleeping on the bare ground,
dhp141:3: Nor rubbing with dust, nor sitting on the haunches, can purify that mortal who has not overcome doubt.
dhp142:1: Even though a man be richly adorned, if he walk in peace,
dhp142:2: If he be quiet, subdued, restrained, and chaste,
dhp142:3: And if he refrain from injuring any living being,
dhp142:4: That man is a Brahman, that man is a hermit, that man is a monk.
dhp143:1: Is there a man in this world so restrained by modesty
dhp143:3: That he wards off reproach as a well-bred horse the whip?
dhp144:1: Even as a well-bred horse touched by the whip, so be ye ardent and active.
dhp144:3: By faith, by virtue, by resolution, by meditation, by understanding of the Law,
dhp144:5: Possessing perfect knowledge and behavior, thoughtful, you will rid yourselves of this great suffering.
dhp145:1: Ditch-diggers lead the water, arrow-makers bend their shafts,
dhp145:3: Carpenters bend the wood, good men control themselves.
